banks.detail: October a hold at ~84-85% (CME FedWatch, Oct 21; Kalshi hold 89%) — blackout confirmed, no Fed speakers. December hike ~90%. 20-yr auction (Oct 21): $13B at 5.469% — record high since the tenor's May-2020 reintroduction; tailed WI 5.460% by 0.9bp (4th tail in a row, improved on Sept's 2bp); B/C 2.73 (vs 2.57 Sept); indirects 58.2% (avg 65.2% — soft foreign demand); directs record 31.6%. Dow Jones/WSJ: 'softer-than-expected'; Barron's: little market reaction. 10Y 5.12%, 2Y 4.79% (FRED DGS10/DGS2, Oct 20). The housing soft patch (starts 1.221M miss, pending home sales -7.3% record low, ADP 18.5K) vs the hot inflation week (import prices +8.1% y/y).
banks.summary: The Fed is expected to hold in October, then decide on a hike in December. Recent inflation has run hot, which keeps the dollar supported while markets wait.

December hike ~76% (ECB Watch, ~Oct-15 vintage; the earlier ~88% poll read is stale) — Commerzbank: 'market is pricing in one [hike] for December and slightly more than one additional hike by mid-2027'. Lagarde: no major-wire carry of new rate remarks indexed today. German PPI +6.7% y/y beat (vs 6.2%); EZ final CPI 3.8% confirmed. Eurozone natural gas >EUR 90/MWh (first since Dec 2022) — fresh energy-cost pressure. France: revenue-section vote postponed (first reading to Oct 27; FinMin Lescure floated Article 49.3); OAT 4.948% (+2.9bp, WSJ/Tradeweb); OAT-Bund ~153bp; Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 negative — markets expect a one-notch cut to A1). EUR/USD 1.1233, flat. IMF (Oct 16 regular Europe report): at least one further 25bp ECB hike in 2026 is warranted to keep core inflation contained; 'further tightening likely warranted' beyond 2026. https://www.reuters.com/business/imf-expects-least-one-more-25-bps-ecb-rate-hike-2026-2026-10-16/
banks.summary: The ECB is expected to hold in October and is leaning toward a hike in December, because inflation is at a three-year high. France's budget trouble is the main thing weighing on the euro.

December hike ~80% (Japan Times/Bloomberg, Oct 21, via ex-BoJ executive Maeda, who expects Dec then Mar/Apr) — a step up from the ~73-74% read. Ueda's 'quite close' to 2% leans December, not October. Sep trade deficit -¥536.6bn vs -¥181bn fc (exports +16.7% missed +20.1%). USD/JPY 158.10-158.18, flat — the BOJ hawkish-forecast headline capping the topside.
banks.summary: The BoJ keeps signalling that more rate hikes are coming, probably in December rather than October. Higher Japanese rates would narrow the gap with the US and support the yen.

banks.detail: November 2-3 hike ~42% — LSEG via Marthio (Oct 21); OIS 41-55% post-Hauser; Goldman Sachs flipped to a November-hike call (25bp to 4.85%, 'the fifth of 2026'); CBA/ANZ a coin toss; Westpac expects 4.85%. Hauser called the inflation outlook 'materially worse' (in part on high oil) — the hawkish follow-through repriced Nov from ~30% at week's start. AUD/USD 0.7032 (+0.2-0.3%), a 3-week high. Q3 CPI Oct 28 the pivot. China LPR held for the 17th straight month (1y 3.00%, 5y 3.50%); PBoC to run daily overnight reverse repos Oct 21-Nov 2 (up to ¥1T/day) — first step toward an overnight policy rate.
banks.summary: The RBA's tone has turned more hawkish, hinting rates may not be high enough yet. A hike in November is possible but not expected, and next week's inflation number is the key test.

Bailey's 8am CT fireside: zero major-wire carry of new rate-policy remarks (headline-only: would not discuss monetary policy) — below bar. UK labor beat stands: unemp 4.7% (lowest since mid-2025), wages 3.7%. Greene hawkish: wage disinflation 'has stalled at levels above those consistent with inflation at 2%.' banks.summary: The Bank of England is almost certain to raise rates on November 5, and the debate is already about December. This week's UK jobs and inflation data will shape how far it goes.
